explanations.text:
import json, the shell, the paths, and two neighbours:
[the tool](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py) — the pieces of a file, [the checking of every pin](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:build_anchors) —
and [the project hand](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py), which keeps the map of the whole project


[cmd_map](cmd_map)(request)
    request is what you typed after human map: the name, an optional --block, --verbatim
    when the words are yours, the text on stdin, like `human map src/app.py <<'EOF' … EOF`.

    the tool reads what you typed
    the abstraction's name gets mapped using [name_to_map()](compiler/cli/human/helpers.py:name_to_map)
    if sort type project or human file then it goes to the project hand.
    if sort type folder, it goes to the front door below.
    if sort type file, it goes on with the run.
    

    ●  the tool reads the file and finds its pieces        ([the pieces](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:block_spans))
    │     It climbs to the project folder using [find_root()](compiler/cli/human/helpers.py:find_root) — the one that holds
    │     human/human.json — reads the file once, and notes every named
    │     thing in it with the lines it covers. It does this so a pin can
    │     only point at a real piece.
    │
    ●  the tool picks up what is abstracted already        ([the record](load_map))
    │     In the project's human folder sits a second file. It holds every
    │     abstraction of this file written so far. On the first run it is
    │     empty.
    │
    ●  the tool keeps your own words, when you said so     ([the guard](verbatim_record))
    │     With --verbatim the text is yours: it must come in plain — a pin
    │     in it stops the run, because the pins come after, with retext —
    │     and a copy of it stays beside the entry as its origin, so a later
    │     mending can be measured against it.
    │
    ●  the tool finds the lines the abstraction covers    ([the lines](entry_span))
    │     An abstraction covers the whole file, or one piece when you said
    │     --block. Here the tool notes the first and the last line of what
    │     it covers.
    │
    ●  the tool numbers the abstraction                    ([the number](next_id))
    │     The first one it ever saved is number 1, the next is number 2,
    │     and so on. The number is how you point at it later.
    │
    
   the tool checks:
     every pin must name a real thinkg, 
     no two pins may share their words, 
     [no cycle](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:check_cycle) may run through the abstractions before it, in this map or in any map it reaches.
   if one bad pin then the run stops, and the tool says which was the error.
    
    │
    ●  the second file grows
          The tool saves three things: the words exactly as written, the
          pins inside them, and for each pin the lines of code it points at —
          and the origin, when the words are yours. Then it
          [counts the lines no abstraction points at yet](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:recompute),
          writes the record — for cmd_map.py it is named
          explanation_compiler__cli__human__cmd_map.py.json —, [adds the file to the project's file list](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:register_file),
          and tells you what it saved and how many lines are still bare.
          The code file is never touched.

[map_project](map_project)(request, root):
  root is the project folder which holds human/human.json.

  refuses a --block because a map with no code under it has no pieces of its own.
  [call project_pins()](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:project_pins)
  verify a pin points at a file of the project, or at one block of a file, at an abstraction of a file's map, or at an abstraction of another map with no code under it.
  if a pin that points anywhere else stops the run.
    
  the map the name gave grows
  the abstraction has no lines of its own. 
  the tool writes it and tells you how many pins reach how many files.



# HELPER FUNCTIONS

[load_map](load_map)(map_path, name)
    ●  the tool opens the record at map_path
          Every entry saved so far, checked for its shape. When there is no
          record yet, the tool starts an empty one named after the file.

[entry_span](entry_span)(name, code_name, code_path, spans, n)
    ●  the tool finds the lines a name covers
          The whole file runs from line 1 to line n, its last line. A piece
          runs from its first line to its last. A name that is neither stops
          the run: it is not a block of the file.

[next_id](next_id)(data)
    ●  the tool gives the new entry its number
          One more than the highest number saved. The first is 1, the next
          is 2, and so on — the number you say when you point at it later.

[verbatim_record](verbatim_record)(a, text)
    ●  the tool keeps a copy of your words
          When you said --verbatim, the copy goes beside the entry, and a
          pin in the text is refused. When you did not, it adds nothing.
          The project hand uses the same guard for its own map.

anchors.words: counts the lines no abstraction points at yet
adds the file to the project's file list
